description: RiverFlowDynamics is a Landlab component for two-dimensional river and floodplain flow simulation. It solves depth-averaged shallow-water equations with a finite-volume scheme, using a semi-implicit treatment of water elevation and velocity. Users supply topography, water boundaries, flow parameters and simulation length; the component contains no fixed watershed or historical flood record. The JOSS-linked public Landlab fork is MIT licensed and the article identifies this named component. It can estimate flow depths and velocities for river-crossing or flood-defence scenarios and support comparisons of channel changes. A caveat is that depth averaging cannot represent vertical flow details, and topographic and boundary-condition errors can dominate local flood predictions. This is a component inside a Landlab fork, not a standalone repository, and its source identity should be kept distinct from the general Landlab framework. No catalogue record explicitly covers it. The article and own repository metadata were read, but no hydraulic benchmark or flood case was executed.
